CAUSE: systemd’s `EnvironmentFile` puts `QUOTA_GATED_LANES` in the service process environment at startup. In `app/quota_gate.py`, `_startup_quota_env` captures that value at import time, and `_live_quota_env()` gives it precedence over the freshly parsed `.env` value. So the mtime check can fire and the new value can be parsed, yet the policy still uses the old startup value. In a local shell where the variable is absent from `os.environ`, the `.env` value takes effect.

The code supports this diagnosis: `_live_quota_env()` refreshes on mtime changes, then selects `_startup_quota_env[name]` before `_dotenv_values[name]`. `app/main.py` also calls `load_dotenv()` with its default `override=False`, so it does not replace an existing systemd-provided value. The existing test `test_dotenv_quota_changes_are_applied_without_module_reload` clears the variable from the environment, so it covers the local-shell case but not this systemd case.

The recommended fix is to make quota settings in `.env` authoritative during live reload, falling back to the startup environment only when the key is absent from `.env`. Alternatively, remove this setting from the service’s `EnvironmentFile` so the live `.env` value is used. Add a regression test with the old value in the startup environment and an edited `.env`.

I did not reproduce the production service behavior directly; this diagnosis follows the precedence in the code and the stated observations.
